Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 – 18 April 1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the known theory of relativity.
In what year was Andromeda Galaxy discovered?
Andromeda Galaxy: The Andromeda Galaxy is a barred spiral galaxy and is the nearest major galaxy to the Milky Way.
Pillars of Creation: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. The astronomers responsible for the photo were Jeff Hester and Paul Scowen from Arizona State University.
Which company manufactures KAI T-50 Golden Eagle?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Korea Aerospace Industries. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
Which country is Yakovlev MC-21 based from?
Yakovlev MC-21: Russia. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Who is credited with discovering Livermorium?
Livermorium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Who is credited with discovering Fentanyl?
Fentanyl: Paul Janssen. Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.
Who is credited with discovering Arsenic?
Arsenic: Albertus Magnus. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
An economist who once worked for the IMF and later served as Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire from 1990 to 1993, this politician has been the country's president since 2010 — name this leader?
Alassane Ouattara (French; born 1 January 1942) is an Ivorian politician and economist who has been President of Ivory Coast (Cte d'Ivoire) since 2010.
Whether from too few red blood cells or faulty hemoglobin, this disorder leaves the blood less able to carry oxygen — often felt as quiet tiredness long before any paleness shows — what is it?
Anemia (also spelt anaemia in British English) is a blood disorder in which the blood has a reduced ability to carry oxygen.
Sharing chemistry with phosphorus and antimony, this group-15 metalloid carries the symbol As and a notorious reputation for toxicity — what is it?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.

This genus of deciduous trees includes 14 species across two subgenera, one found only in East Asia with low, multi-trunked growth, the other spanning Europe, Asia, and eastern North America. What tree genus is this?

Beech (genus Fagus) is a genus of deciduous trees in the family Fagaceae, native to subtropical (accessory forest element) and temperate (as dominant element of mesophytic forests) Eurasia and North America.
As Square's chief technology officer, this software engineer helped build Cash App before he was fatally stabbed in San Francisco in 2023 — who was he?
Bob Lee (businessman) (December 20, 1979 - April 4, 2023) was an American businessman and software engineer who was best known for helping to create the financial service Cash App.
Located between the lower back and the perineum, these two rounded regions of human anatomy are built around the gluteus maximus — the largest muscle in the human body — name this body part?
Buttocks (sing.: buttock) are two rounded portions of the exterior anatomy of humans, located on the posterior of the pelvic region.
Portuguese explorers carried this tropical American tree to India in the 16th century; today Ivory Coast and India lead a 3.9-million-ton global harvest of its nut — what is it?
Cashew is the common name of a tropical evergreen tree Anacardium occidentale, in the family Anacardiaceae.
The first element in group 6, it lends its name to the shiny plating on car bumpers and, mixed into steel, makes it stainless. Which steely-grey metal is it?
Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
This bird's name comes from the Quechua word 'kuntur,' and its California-dwelling relative was nearly wiped out by habitat loss — which giant vulture soars over the Andes?
Condor is the common name for two genera of New World vultures, each with one extant species.
As of December 2025 worth an estimated $8.7 billion, this Swedish businessman founded and chairs a massive music-streaming company — who is he?
Daniel Ek (Swedish; born 21 February 1983) is a Swedish businessman and technologist.
Found in nighttime cold remedies like NyQuil and paired with vitamin B6 for pregnancy-related nausea, this antihistamine is an inverse agonist at the H1 receptor — which drug?
Doxylamine is an antihistamine medication used to treat insomnia and allergies, and - in combination with pyridoxine (vitamin B6) - to treat morning sickness in pregnant women.
This inner lining of the uterus thickens each cycle and is shed during menstruation in humans and a handful of other species, including certain bats and shrews — what is it?
Endometrium is the inner lining of the uterus (womb) in mammals.
Cats in this subfamily can purr but never roar, thanks to a bony rather than flexible hyoid bone — which subfamily?
Felinae are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.

A French economist who gave lectures up and down the country and helped found the Inter-Parliamentary Union, he shared the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901 for his work in Europe's peace movement — who was he?
Frédéric Passy (20 May 1822 - 12 June 1912) was a French economist and pacifist who was a founding member of several peace societies and the Inter-Parliamentary Union.
This week-long 2010 manhunt across Tyne and Wear and Northumberland ended when the fugitive shot himself following a six-hour standoff near Rothbury. What event is it?
Goose (pl.: geese) is a bird of any of several waterfowl species in the family Anatidae.

Linked to conditions like tuberculosis, bronchitis, and lung cancer, this medical term describes blood discharged from the airway rather than internal bleeding elsewhere in the body. What is it called?
Hemoptysis is the discharge of blood or blood-stained mucus through the mouth coming from the bronchi, larynx, trachea, or lungs.
This negatively charged ion, one oxygen bonded to one hydrogen, acts as a base and forms industrially vital salts like the sodium version used to make millions of tons of chemicals. What ion is it?
Hydroxide (occasionally hydroxyl ion) is a diatomic anion with chemical formula OH.
One of the largest dog breeds in the world, this sighthound was historically used to course game and became the official mascot of a British Guards regiment in 1902. What breed is it?
Irish Wolfhound is a breed of large sighthound that has, by its presence and substantial size, inspired literature, poetry and mythology.
This Johns Hopkins psychologist coined the terms 'gender role' and 'sexual orientation' and believed gender was malleable during a child's first two years. Who was he?
John Money (8 July 1921 - 7 July 2006) was a New Zealand American psychologist, sexologist and professor at Johns Hopkins University known for his research on human sexual behavior and gender.
These paired folds of skin are the major externally visible structures of the vulva, with an outer 'majora' set and an inner 'minora' set — what are they called?
Labia are the major externally visible structures of the vulva. In other mammals, the labia majora are not present and the labia minora are instead referred to as the labia vulvae.

The second woman to earn a physics doctorate from the University of Vienna, this Austrian-Swedish scientist became the first female full physics professor in Germany — and was instrumental in discovering nuclear fission. Who is she?
Lise Meitner (7 November 1878 - 27 October 1968) was an Austrian and Swedish nuclear physicist who was instrumental in the discovery of nuclear fission.

Made by every living organism and responsible for much of the sour taste in fruit, this dicarboxylic food additive's salt form also serves as a key intermediate in the cell's central metabolic energy cycle — what compound is it?
Malic acid is an organic compound with the molecular formula HO2CCH(OH)CH2CO2H.

This mammal family, uniting skunks and stink badgers, is defined by highly developed scent glands used to ward off predators, and was only split from the weasel family in the 1990s — what family is it?
Mephitidae is a family of mammals comprising the skunks and stink badgers.
This unique group of mammals is the only one whose members lay eggs rather than bear live young, comprising the platypus and four echidna species — what group is it?
Monotreme are mammals of the order Monotremata.

First arising in wormlike creatures some 550 million years ago, this body-wide network coordinates actions and relays sensory signals through a central half and a peripheral half — what system is being described?
Nervous system is the highly complex part of an animal that coordinates its actions and sensory information by transmitting signals to and from different parts of its body.
Beginning in the embryo and maturing a primary oocyte into a fertilization-ready egg cell, what is this reproductive process called?
Oogenesis is the differentiation of the ovum (egg cell) into a cell competent to further develop when fertilized.
Native to the islands of Southeast Asia, this bushy perennial herb in the mint family is prized for a fragrant essential oil used widely in perfumery — what plant is it?
Patchouli (also spelled patchouly or pachouli; Pogostemon cablin) is a species of flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, commonly called the mint or deadnettle family.

First described in 1850, this family of over 2,000 araneomorph spiders includes the cellar spider and the "vibrating spider" — and lends the nickname "daddy long-legs" to one of its species; what is the family?
Pholcidae are a family of araneomorph spiders. The family, first described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, is divided into 94 genera.
Native to Southeast Asia and a natural, non-hybrid ancestor of both the grapefruit and the bitter orange, this largest of all citrus fruits also goes by the name 'shaddock' — what is it?
Pomelo (PUM-; or pummelo, Citrus maxima), also known as a shaddock, is the largest citrus fruit.
This opening at the center of the iris lets light reach the retina and appears black — round in people, a slit in cats, and even a ring shape in some catfish — what's it called?
Pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.
Named from Greek words for 'rose' and 'tree,' this genus of over 1,000 woody flowering plant species serves as the national flower of Nepal and the state flower of Washington — what is it?

Rhododendron (pl.: rhododendra), from Ancient Greek (rhdon), meaning "rose", and (dndron), meaning "tree", is a very large genus of about 1,024 species of woody plants in the heath family (Ericaceae).
The FAO/WHO Codex standard recognizes 21 species under this common name for small silvery forage fish, distinguished from their larger 'pilchard' cousins mainly by size — what fish is it?
Sardine are common names for various species of small, oily forage fish in the herring suborder Clupeoidei.

Developed by the Chukchi people in the Russian Far East for pulling sleds and companionship, this medium-sized Spitz-family dog breed is smaller than the similar-looking Alaskan Malamute — name the breed?
Siberian Husky is a breed of medium-sized working sled dog.
The largest order of reptiles, this group is set apart by movable quadrate bones that let snakes gape their jaws around oversized prey — what's the order called?
Squamata (Latin squamatus, 'scaly, having scales') is the largest order of reptiles; most members of which are commonly known as lizards, with the group also including snakes.

This medical term describes a resting heart rate above 100 beats per minute in adults, which can be either a normal exercise response or a sign of an electrical problem in the heart — what's the condition called?
Tachycardia is a heart rate that exceeds the normal resting rate.
This viral brain infection, transmitted through the bite of infected parasitic arachnids, saw its European case count climb almost 400% over three decades. What is this arachnid-spread illness?
Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a viral infectious disease involving the central nervous system, transmitted by the bite of several species of infected ticks.
With 92 protons and half-lives stretching up to 4.5 billion years, this radioactive metal is handy for dating the age of the Earth — which silvery-grey element?
Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.
His 1925 Umdeutung paper reinterpreted old quantum theory, and two years later he published a famous uncertainty principle — which German physicist was he?

Werner Heisenberg (5 December 1901 - 1 February 1976) was a German theoretical physicist, one of the main pioneers of the theory of quantum mechanics and a principal scientist in the German nuclear program during World War II.
Launched in 1981 as a joint venture between French and Italian aerospace firms, this high-wing turboprop airliner later formed the basis for a stretched successor introduced in 1989 — which aircraft?
This mushroom genus of more than 400 species includes both the common button mushroom and the field mushroom, the two most-cultivated fungi in the West — which genus is it?
Approved for medical use in the US in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowers uric acid to prevent gout and certain kidney stones — what medication is it?
Allopurinol: Medication. Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.

Found along the Andes and Pacific coasts of South America, this enormous New World vulture is one of the largest flying birds by wingspan, with males sporting a fleshy comb atop a bald red head — which species is it?
Andean condor: Species of bird. The Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
First described by Linnaeus in 1753, this Old World vegetable — better known on dinner plates as celery — is also cultivated for a bulbous root form called celeriac. What is its scientific name?

One of its founders, James Keeler, said this science 'seeks to ascertain the nature of the heavenly bodies... rather than their positions or motions' — studying everything from the Sun to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
Named by naturalist Constantine Rafinesque in 1815, this predatory saltwater fish prowls near coral reefs and is a favorite target of sport anglers worldwide — what is it?

Having evolved independently at least 94 separate times — first in octocorals some 540 million years ago — this living glow lights up fireflies, deep-sea fish, fungi and dinoflagellates alike; what is it?
Bioluminescence: Emission of light by a living organism.

Despite lacking the tight head of typical cabbage, this leafy Chinese vegetable has a flavor often compared to spinach and water chestnuts, with a milder white bulb and stronger-tasting green leaves — what vegetable is it?
Bok choy: Subspecies of flowering plant.
With a large head, deep facial folds, and a flat face with a jutting lower jaw, this British breed's ancestors were once used for baiting cattle before the sport was banned in 1835 — which breed?
Bulldog: British breed of dog. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.
Indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains and grown across Asia and Africa largely for hashish production, this plant species carries far more THC than industrial hemp — which species is it?
Cannabis indica: Species of plant. Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Its edible 'curd' is actually a dense head of undeveloped flower buds, and one variety grows its curds in spiral fractal patterns — which vegetable?
Cauliflower: Vegetable in the species Brassica oleracea.
Her famous experiment proved parity is not conserved — earning Lee and Yang the 1957 Nobel while she received the inaugural Wolf Prize in Physics instead. Which Manhattan Project physicist was she?
This genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria found in soil and animal intestines includes the microbes responsible for both botulism and tetanus — which genus?
Clostridium: Genus of bacteria. Species of Clostridium inhabit soils and the intestinal tracts of animals, including humans.
This towering annual in the daisy family yields the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil, plus snackable seeds and birdseed — and its wild cousins sprout multiple flower heads. What is it?
Common sunflower: Species of flowering plant in the family of Asteraceae.
This genus of some 100 low-growing perennials gives us saffron from the dried stigmas of one autumn-blooming species — name the flower genus?
This basic unit of time — averaging 24 hours, or 86,400 seconds — marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun, and got split into weeks, months, and years. What is it?
Day: Time of one rotation around a planet axis.

Governed since 1961 by the Vienna Convention, this practice of using official representatives to influence international relations became a professionalized field in the early 20th century. What is it?
Diplomacy: Practice of conducting negotiations between representatives of groups or states.
Starting life bilaterally symmetrical as larvae but growing into five-pointed radial adults, this animal phylum includes starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers — what is it called?
Echinoderm: Marine phylum of animals often with radial symmetries.
This branch of zoology, whose name derives from Greek words for 'insect' and 'study,' covers a field that has described over 1.3 million species — which discipline?
The only Old World member of its family to breed in the Northern Hemisphere's temperate zones, this migratory songbird winters in central and southern Africa — what is it?
Eurasian golden oriole: Species of bird.
This Swiss thinker, alongside Charles Sanders Peirce, is considered one of the two founders of semiotics — the field he himself called 'semiology' — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure: Swiss linguist and philosopher (1857–1913)
Marked by physical traits such as a long face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, this inherited neurodevelopmental disorder stems from a repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene — which condition?
Fragile X syndrome: X-linked dominant genetic disorder.
This is the largest lizard family, boasting over 950 species that cling to surfaces via Van der Waals forces in their toe hairs — including house, tokay, and day varieties — which family?
Gekkonidae: Family of lizards. Gekkonidae (the common geckos) is the largest family of geckos, containing over 950 described species in 62 genera.
Caused by iodine deficiency in over 90% of cases worldwide, this neck swelling results from an enlarged thyroid gland — what's the condition called?
Goitre: Neck swelling due to enlarged thyroid gland. A goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.
After a record 43 years as crown prince, this Swedish monarch approved constitutional reforms stripping the crown of its remaining political powers shortly before his 1973 death. Who was he?
Gustaf VI Adolf: King of Sweden from 1950 to 1973.

This airway symptom — blood or blood-streaked mucus coughed up from the lungs or throat — turns dangerous mainly because of choking rather than blood loss once it passes 300 milliliters. What is it called?
Damage to the sympathetic trunk nerves produces this trio of symptoms on one side of the face — a constricted pupil, a droopy eyelid, and reduced sweating — what is this condition called?
Horner's syndrome: Facial disorder due to damage of the sympathetic nerves.

When the thyroid produces too little hormone, the body slows down — cold intolerance, fatigue, constipation, weight gain — and worldwide too little dietary iodine is the leading cause. What's the condition?
Hypothyroidism: Insufficient production of thyroid hormones.
This ring-shaped structure in the eye controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the size of the pupil — and it's also what determines eye color — what is it?
Iris (anatomy): Colored part of an eye.
Son of Taiwanese immigrants, this engineer launched the world's most valuable company from a Denny's restaurant in 1993 after earning a Stanford master's degree — who is he?
Jensen Huang: Taiwanese and American businessman (born 1963)
Nicknamed the 'miracle leaf' and 'life plant,' this Madagascar-native succulent sprouts tiny new plantlets right along the edges of its leaves — which species?

Kalanchoe pinnata: Succulent plant native to Madagascar. Kalanchoe pinnata, commonly known as cathedral bells, air plant, life plant, miracle leaf, and love bush, is a succulent plant native to Madagascar.

Native to the tropical Americas, this flowering shrub was carried to Europe by Dutch explorers and later brought to Goa by the Portuguese, becoming a notorious invasive weed across some 50 countries — which plant?
Lantana camara: Species of plant. Lantana camara (common lantana) is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family (Verbenaceae), native to the tropics of the Americas.
Named after the Italian word for lemon, this citrus-scented compound comes in two mirror-image forms — one smelling of oranges, the other like pine — what is it?

Born into one of Europe's richest families in Vienna, this philosopher studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge before giving away his inheritance and enlisting in the Austro-Hungarian Army — who is he?
Ludwig Wittgenstein: Austrian philosopher and logician (1889–1951)

First isolated in the 1770s and carrying atomic number 25, this hard, silvery transition metal is a key alloying agent in stainless steel and also an essential trace nutrient in the human diet — which element?
Manganese: Chemical element with atomic number 25 (Mn)

Co-inventor of a heart-valve repair device called the MitraClip, this Turkish-American cardiac surgeon became a famous TV health personality before being named the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services in 2025 — who is he?
Mehmet Oz: American TV host and government official (born 1960)
Sitting atop the brainstem and linking it to the diencephalon and cerebrum, this structure governs vision, hearing, motor control, and arousal -- what is it called?
Midbrain: Forward-most portion of the brainstem.
Native to tropical Central and South America, this genus of 59 flowering plant species belongs to the arum family — which genus?
NASA was formed in 1958 by absorbing which older federal aeronautics body?
The National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics had run American aeronautical research since 1915. The Space Race turned it into a space agency.
Present in 26 African countries with one of its largest undisturbed populations at Kenya's Lake Turkana, which large crocodilian sees adult males reach 3.5 to 5 metres long?
This British engineer rewrote Maxwell's equations into the form we use today and devised the telegrapher's equations — who was he?
Oliver Heaviside: British mathematician and electrical engineer (1850–1925)
Discovered in 1802 and named after a newly found asteroid, this silvery-white platinum-group metal is prized for cleaning up automobile exhaust in catalytic converters — which element?
Palladium: Chemical element with atomic number 46 (Pd)

Famous for the giant throat pouch beneath its long beak, this large water bird's eight living species range from the tropics to temperate zones, with some even flying inland to Australia's Red Centre after heavy rains — what bird is this?
Pelican: Genus of large water birds with a throat pouch.
With a phosphate-charged head and two fatty-acid tails joined by glycerol, this molecule builds neuron membranes and can decline up to 20% by age 80 — what is it?
Sitting less than a degree from the north celestial pole, this yellow supergiant is famously steady for navigation — but is secretly a triple star system. What is it?
Polaris: Northern pole-star; brightest star in Ursa Minor.

Diagnosed in about 8% of male urology visits in the US, this umbrella term covers several bacterial and non-bacterial pelvic conditions, despite its name not always involving actual inflammation — which condition?
Prostatitis: Medical condition. Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.
Sold as Seroquel and prescribed for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, this atypical antipsychotic is also widely (and questionably) used as a sleep aid for its tranquillizing effect — which drug?
Quetiapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Quetiapine is believed to work by blocking a number of receptors, including those for serotonin and dopamine.
Native to East Asia but a notorious invasive pest in Europe and North America, this knotweed has won over beekeepers and foragers alike, its young stems tasting of lemony rhubarb. What plant is it?
Native to Eurasia and commonly known simply as the raspberry, this red-fruited bramble is widely cultivated across temperate regions — what species is it?
Nicknamed 'snail fever,' this tropical disease is caused by a parasitic flatworm picked up from freshwater contaminated by infected snails — what is it?
Schistosomiasis: Human disease caused by parasitic worms called schistosomes.

Recognized by the Kennel Club in 1909, this small, clever herding dog breed originated in Scotland's northern isles and was originally called by a different collie name before breeders objected — which breed?
Shetland Sheepdog: Scottish breed of dog. The Shetland Sheepdog, also known as the Sheltie, is a breed of herding dog that originated in the Shetland Islands of Scotland.

Originating in South America and rapidly diversifying after the extinction of the dinosaurs, this plant family — commonly known as the nightshades — includes toxic alkaloid-rich species alongside tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers. What family is it?
This English clergyman was the first person ever to measure blood pressure, and on the side he invented a ventilator and even wrote a tract against drinking — who was he?
Stephen Hales: English clergyman and scientist (1677–1761)
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'concurrence,' this medical term describes a set of signs and symptoms that tend to occur together — what is it called?
Syndrome: Association of several clinically recognizable features.
Also sold under the name dronabinol, this principal psychoactive compound in cannabis is prescribed to relieve chemotherapy-induced nausea and HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss — what is it?
Tetrahydrocannabinol: Psychoactive component of cannabis. It is the principal psychoactive constituent of Cannabis and one of at least 113 total cannabinoids identified on the plant.
Sitting between cells and organs in the body's organization, this assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix takes its English name from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology): Group of similar cells performing a specific function.
Roughly three times stiffer than steel and nearly as hard as diamond, this gray powder is sintered into cutting tools, armor-piercing bullets, and jewelry — what compound is it?
Tungsten carbide: Hard, dense and stiff chemical compound.
The brightest star in the constellation Lyra, this star sits just 25 light-years away and served as Earth's northern pole star around 12,000 BCE — which star?
Vega: Brightest star in the constellation Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
With a distinctive pale eye and grey nape against black plumage, this small, gregarious member of the crow family was first formally described by Linnaeus — name the bird?
Western jackdaw: Species of bird in the crow family Corvidae.
Also called the pikeperch, this ray-finned game fish native to western Eurasian waters is the type species that gave its whole genus a name — which fish?
Zander: Species of fish. The zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
What is the chemical symbol for sulfur?
The symbol for sulfur is S. Sulfur, also spelled as sulphur, is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
What is the chemical symbol for rubidium?
The symbol for rubidium is Rb. Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.
